decisionsTitle: A «Direcționare» checkpoint, and the cut-off as a time limit from the start
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-14, with a screenshot of «Adaugă puncte» in the checkpoints card:** «aici aș vrea să am și un tip de punct de tipul „direcționare”». And a few minutes later, on the cut-off box: «în loc de ora limită, trebuie să punem „timp limită” ca să fie dinamic». Later, of the open points: «it's YOLO man» — the lane decided them and says what it decided below. Amends §757 (the cut-off as a time of the day on the event's clock, the five kinds' set, the table's «Ora limită», the file's version 2, the bib's clock), §763 (the card's boxes name their form — two more) and §751 (the event's file).

**A fifth kind, «Direcționare» / "Direction"** — a volunteer who shows the way at a junction. `DIRECTION` joins the enum `event_checkpoint_kind` (migration `0153`, expand only: `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`, in a file of its own because PostgreSQL refuses to use a new value in the transaction that adds it). It is the card's fifth tick in «Ce găsești aici», a chip on the event page with its own glyph — the road sign with its arrow, `Directions` from the installed icon set, one glyph per kind so the chips tell them apart — and a waypoint of a GPX whose name, symbol or type says a junction, a turn, a signpost, a marshal, «direcționare», «intersecție», «bifurcație» (`kindsFromWords`). **The bib's strip draws it as a dot**, like first aid and timing: the strip draws only the two things a runner takes, a cup and a fork, and a person showing the way is not one; the point still has its tick, its kilometre and, with the second tick, its clock. The kinds column is an array, so nothing else moved.

**The cut-off is «Timp limită»: minutes from the start, not a time of the day.** §757 stored a time of day on the event's clock so a moved date kept it; the owner's point is the opposite one, that the club knows how long the last runner may take and the clock should follow the start. `event_checkpoints.cutoff_minutes` (migration `0154`, expand only: `integer`, `CHECK` 1 to 10080, the week the race's own box may hold) is what is written now; `cutoff_time` stays, unwritten and unread, until a later contract release. **The minutes count from the race's gun when it has one, else the event's start** — the instant the race's own «Timp limită» counts from (`duration.ts#durationBase`) — and they are elapsed minutes, so a point's limit and the event's are compared as minutes against minutes: no clock arithmetic, no wrap past midnight, and the night the clocks change moves nothing. The migration filled the column from the old rows by the same rule in SQL (`UPDATE … FROM`): the gun's hour on the event's clock, a cut-off at or before it left empty, a cut-off earlier than the start's hour read as the next day's only for an event whose end, counted from the start, runs past midnight, every cut-off of an event whose start has no date or no hour left empty (§545) — **the club retypes those as «Timp limită»** (an event whose hour is «se anunță mai târziu» that already held a cut-off; §757 shipped a day earlier, so there should be few or none). A test runs it on real PostgreSQL (PGlite) with a point before and after the gun, a night race, summer time and an unknown start, and holds every answer to the platform's one converter.

**One converter** (`domain/start.ts`): `cutoffClockOf(start, minutes, zone)` says the clock a limit closes at, `checkpointClock` / `withCutoffClocks` give a reader the clocks of the event it draws, and `minutesFromClock` reads a time of day back as minutes — used by the old file's import, and mirrored by the migration. `cutoffOffset` is gone. The clock is derived and never stored; `listCheckpoints` joins the event and hands every reader the same one (the card, the bib, the file), and the public page and the staff's preview recompute it from the event they draw, so a draft's start shows its own.

**The card's box** is the race's own two boxes, «Ore» and «Minute», **the same component** (`DurationBoxes`, extracted from «Când și unde», its words, its limits — hours up to a week's worth, minutes to 59 — and its recall of what a refusal kept), under «Timp limită» with the help «De la start: până atunci trebuie să treacă ultimul alergător. Lasă gol dacă nu e limită.» A second duration widget was refused. Both boxes name the card's form (`form=`, §763) through the house's `RecallField`; with scripts off the plain post works as before. **Refused:** a limit that is not a duration (zero, sixty minutes, a letter) naming the box; a limit longer than the event's own «Timp limită», saying both durations; a limit longer than the one of a point further along; and **a limit while the start has no date or hour to count it from** — «Timpul limită … se numără de la start, iar startul nu are încă o oră». The refusal says to write the start's hour **and save the event** first, because the card's form posts no event field. The decision on that last case: a saved limit posted unchanged is kept while the hour is «se anunță mai târziu» (the club can still save a note), and the event's own save is held to it by minutes only, because a duration stays true when the hour is unsaid — only the clock stops being said, so shortening «Timp limită» under a saved point's limit is refused then too, and so is an imported file whose point is longer than its race. Clearing only the hours box of a whole-hour limit removes the limit instead of refusing a «0»; «crossing» in a waypoint's name, «fork» alone and «ghid» no longer say «Direcționare» (a symbol «Crossing» still does). **Moving the start or the gun is no longer refused**: it moves every clock and no limit, which is the point; the refusal «ora limită nu e după start» went with the time of day, and the event save is held only for a shortened «Timp limită» under a saved limit and a shortened route (§757).

**The page and the bib say the same words.** A checkpoint's line reads «Timp limită: 1 h 30 min · se închide la 11:30» («Time limit: 1 h 30 min · closes at 11:30»), and only «Timp limită: 1 h 30 min» while the start has no hour; a point without one reads «fără timp limită». The finish row says the event's limit the same way, «Timp limită: 2 h 30 min · se închide la 12:30». The bib's strip prints the clock through the same converter with «…cu orele limită» (the tick keeps its name: what is printed on paper is an hour); the pictures' stamp now holds the minutes, the clock and, in the database stamp, the gun and the zone, so a moved start is a new picture address.

**The event's file is version 3**: a checkpoint carries `cutoffMinutes`. Versions 1 and 2 are still read (`upgradeCheckpoints`, after `upgradeVersion1`): a time of day is converted to minutes by the one converter when the file says the event's start — the gun's, else the date and hour — and the clock is after it; otherwise it is left out. **A kind this release does not know is left out too. Neither is ever a refusal of the file**: the import's preview, the diff and the result say it in words («La punctele de control din fișier s-au lăsat deoparte tipurile pe care această versiune nu le știe (în total: N).» and «… orele limită care nu se puteau număra de la start (în total: N). Scrie-le din nou ca „Timp limită”.»), and a file made before «Direcționare» existed reads with its four kinds and nothing to say. The rules that need the event (a kilometre within the route, a limit not longer than the event's, in order, with a start to count from) are still the import's to apply, refusing the whole file before anything is written.

**Refused:** storing a clock and deriving the minutes (the owner asked for the reverse; a stored clock is the §757 answer that did not follow the start); counting minutes on the wall clock (the night the clocks change would move a limit by an hour for nobody's reason); a second duration widget in the card; a glyph for «Direcționare» drawn on the bib's strip (a cup and a fork are what a runner takes); a migration that clears `cutoff_time` (that is a contract, for a later release, when nothing reads it).
changelogLine: - **A «Direcționare» checkpoint, and the cut-off as «Timp limită»** — a fifth kind for the person who shows the way, with a road-sign glyph; a point's cut-off is now typed as hours and minutes from the start, in the race's own boxes, and the page says «Timp limită: 1 h 30 min · se închide la 11:30», so moving the start moves every clock. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 77. Given an event with checkpoints, when its page renders, then a point's line reads «Timp limită: 1 h 30 min · se închide la 11:30» («Time limit: 1 h 30 min · closes at 11:30») — the minutes from the gun (else the start) and the clock they fall at on the event's clock, only «Timp limită: 1 h 30 min» while the start has no hour — or a dash read as «fără timp limită», never «Ora limită»; the finish row says the event's limit the same way, «Timp limită: 2 h 30 min · se închide la 12:30»; a point's kinds are chips each with a glyph and its word, «Direcționare» / "Direction" among them with the road sign's glyph, one glyph per kind (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 88. With «…cu orele limită», «km 12 · 11:30» prints the clock a point's time limit closes at, computed from the event's start by the same converter the event page uses; a «Direcționare» point is a dot like first aid and timing; the bibs page's, the preview's and the desk's picture addresses change when a checkpoint's kilometre, kinds, time limit or the clock it closes at changes, so also when the start or the gun moves (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 123. Given the event editor, when an Organizer, an Administrator or a Superadministrator saves «Puncte de control», then each point's kinds come from «Apă», «Mâncare», «Prim ajutor», «Cronometrare», «Direcționare», and its «Timp limită» is typed in the race's own two boxes, «Ore» and «Minute» (the same component and limits as the race's), with the help «De la start: până atunci trebuie să treacă ultimul alergător. Lasă gol dacă nu e limită.»; the limit is a positive duration of at most a week counted from the gun (else the start), not longer than the event's own «Timp limită», not longer than a farther point's, and needs a start with a date and an hour — a refusal names the hours box (the minutes box when that is the one), says both durations and keeps what was typed, with scripts on and off — while a saved limit posted unchanged stays when the hour is to be announced; every box of the card names the card's form (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 127. Given an event with saved checkpoints, when an event save, a series save reaching other dates, or an import over the event that does not replace the list would end the event («Timp limită») before a saved point's time limit — also while the start's hour is to be announced, the comparison being minutes against minutes — or shorten the route under a saved point, then the save is refused naming «Puncte de control» with the rule's own sentence (and the date, on another date of a series) and nothing is written; moving the start or the gun is never refused: every clock follows it and no time limit changes; a start whose hour is then to be announced keeps the saved limits and says no clock (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 126 and 129. The event's JSON file is version 3: a checkpoint carries `cutoffMinutes`, minutes from the start (the gun on a race), and no time of day; a file of version 1 or 2 is read and its time of day converted by the platform's one converter when the file says the event's start (the gun's, else the date and hour) and the clock is after it, otherwise left out; a kind the release does not know is left out; neither refuses the file — the preview, the diff and the result say how many were left out — and a file made before «Direcționare» reads with its four kinds (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the database, then `event_checkpoint_kind` has the value `DIRECTION` and `event_checkpoints.cutoff_minutes` holds a positive integer of at most 10080 or null; the migration that added the column filled it from `cutoff_time` through the event's gun (a point after the gun counted from it, one at or before it left empty, a night race counted across midnight, an event whose start has no hour or no date left empty), keeps `cutoff_time` as it was, and is safe to run twice; a GPX waypoint whose words say a junction, a turn, a signpost or a marshal is offered as «Direcționare» (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: a «Direcționare» checkpoint; its cut-off as a time limit from the gun
